title: model-loading-weights-shard-debug-scratchpad-maya-chen
content:
Context:
- Trying to load 30B model for Dedicated staging cluster (stg-dedicated-02). Model originally exported by optimizer pipeline v2.1 -> produced checkpoint with 8 shards (weights-0000..0007.safetensors) + manifest.json. Workload: low-latency chat, runtime uses continuous KV cache and streaming.
- Symptoms: model load fails during weights download/verification. Error occurs ~30s into load (after first few shards). Fail seems nondeterministic across restarts (sometimes fails on shard 0003, sometimes 0005).

What I tried (commands & outputs):
1) Basic svc download (from S3):
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/exports/ops-30b-v2/weights-0003.safetensors /tmp/weights-0003.safetensors --region us-west-2
   -> completes successfully locally (size 1.2GB)
   sha256sum /tmp/weights-0003.safetensors
   -> got: e3b0c44298fc... (example)

2) Runtime fetch (container) using internal presigned URL (curl):
   curl -f -L "${PRESIGNED_URL}" -o /tmp/weights-0003.safetensors
   -> sometimes returns HTTP 200 then the runtime logs: "Checksum mismatch for shard weights-0003.safetensors (expected: e3b0..., got: 9f7a...)"

3) rclone check between S3 bucket and local copy:
   rclone md5sum s3:redwood-models/exports/ops-30b-v2 | grep weights-0003
   -> rclone lists md5 that matches local file.

4) Tried fetching via internal artifact proxy (artifact-service v1.4):
   curl -v http://artifact-proxy.internal/weights/ops-30b-v2/weights-0003.safetensors -o /tmp/a && sha256sum /tmp/a
   -> sometimes connection reset (RST) mid-download. Logs from proxy: "Upstream S3 connection timed out; retried 2/3"

5) Replayed load with DEBUG logs enabled in serving-runtime:
   - runtime printed: "opening shard 0003, expected_size=1298341120"
   - bytes_read reported as equal to expected_size
   - then verify_sha256 failed: expected e3b0..., got 9f7a...
   - stack: model_loader->shard_verifier->download_stream_reader

6) Local checksum of file downloaded directly from S3 (aws cli) matches manifest.json sha256. But file downloaded via presigned URL sometimes yields different sha256.

Error snippets (from runtime logs):
- "ERROR model_loader: checksum mismatch for shard weights-0003.safetensors (expected sha256=e3b0c44298..., got sha256=9f7a1c3f...)"
- "WARN artifact_proxy: upstream S3 transient error: 504 Gateway Timeout"
- "ERROR model-loader: failed to assemble checkpoint: incomplete shards (missing verification for 0003)"

Hypotheses / notes:
- H1: Artifact storage has inconsistent object versions (S3 eventual consistency for overwrite). Some presigned URLs point to a partially uploaded/old object. But aws cli cp to same key returns correct object -> less likely unless proxy using different key/prefix.
- H2: Artifact proxy performs streaming transfer and transforms (e.g., chunked encoding, gzip) incorrectly leading to content corruption for some chunk boundaries. Proxy logs show connection timeouts/retries which might cause partial reassembly.
- H3: Network middleboxes or container runtime (envoy sidecar) are truncating or re-chunking range requests; checksum fails even if file sizes match due to reordering.
- H4: Upstream build pipeline sometimes generates corrupt shard (bad upload); but direct S3 check via aws cli matched manifest so probably not this for the known object we tested.
- H5: Checksum algorithm mismatch: manifest contains sha256 of raw safetensors file, but runtime computes sha256 over streamed bytes after decompression or after some header stripped. Confirmed runtime uses raw bytes -> seems consistent.

Repro steps (what reproduces):
- Start serving-runtime container in staging with DEBUG logging and ARTIFACT_PROXY enabled.
- Trigger model load via admin API: POST /admin/models/load {model: ops-30b-v2}
- Watch logs: failures typically appear within 20-40s.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Bypassed proxy by injecting S3 credentials into container and letting runtime download directly -> model loads successfully on first try (suggests proxy is implicated).
- Increased artifact-proxy retry/wait config -> reduced frequency but not eliminated.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Get full tcpdump from runtime -> to see if bytes differ in-flight. (blocked: need SRE approval for packet capture in staging)
- [ ] Ask infra to check artifact-proxy logs around the timestamps (09/12 14:02:xx). Clip sent to Jordan.
- [ ] Add sha256 header propagation in artifact-proxy to compare upstream/downstream bytes on proxy (small code change).
- [ ] Try serving-runtime download with range requests disabled (force single GET) to rule out chunking bugs.
- [ ] Investigate Envoy sidecar config for HTTP/1.1 chunk encoding / content-length rewriting.
- [ ] If proxy is root cause, plan: patch to stream without re-chunking and add end-to-end hash verification.
- [ ] If corruption persists even bypassing proxy, run filesystem-level checks (EBS/EFS) and checksum the mounted file system.

Questions for the team / notes to self:
- Does artifact-proxy perform any transformations (gzip, decompress, re-chunk)? Jordan: "No intentional transforms, but uses http client library that may re-chunk responses".
- Does signing presigned URL include versionId? If not, overwritten objects could be served. Confirmed current keys do not include versionId. Consider switching to versioned keys for uploads.
- Should we require content-hash metadata as object/user metadata on upload? That would let proxy compare immediately.

Linked traces / tickets:
- JIRA-INF-3421: "stg-dedicated model load checksum errors" (assigned to Jordan)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/278 (adds verbose shard verification logging)
- Slack: #infra-artifact-service thread: "artifact-proxy transient corruption" (09/12)

Notes after talking to Jordan (09/13):
- He saw artifact-proxy drop into a fallback codepath when S3 returned 504 which caused the proxy to re-GET with different client settings; double-GET codepath used a streaming buffer that didn't reset correctly between attempts (possible bug). He'll submit a small fix to reset buffer and add tests.

If fix is deployed:
- Monitor model load attempts for next 48h in staging. If stable -> schedule backport to prod artifact-proxy (low-risk patch).

Unresolved:
- Why did direct presigned URL sometimes return bad bytes while aws cli returned correct bytes for the same key? Need to capture headers & versionId to be sure we hit same object.

Quick commands to reproduce locally (for whoever picks this up):
1) aws s3 presign s3://redwood-models/exports/ops-30b-v2/weights-0003.safetensors --expires-in 3600 > url.txt
2) curl -v $(cat url.txt) -o /tmp/curl-weights && sha256sum /tmp/curl-weights
3) aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/exports/ops-30b-v2/weights-0003.safetensors /tmp/aws-weights && sha256sum /tmp/aws-weights
4) Compare checksums. If mismatch, capture tcpdump on host and upload to JIRA ticket.

Bottom line: most evidence points to artifact-proxy streaming/retry logic as the culprit. Prioritize small fix + more robust end-to-end checksum validation in proxy and a rollout to staging.

---
Notes to self: keep this doc as a running breadcrumb trail. If/when resolved, convert this into postmortem draft and include timeline + root cause + customer impact notes.
